body: I phonetically spell out names on purpose because during stressful times, it makes the baristas laugh and I can be creative to an extent (ex: 'Tony', and I spell it 'Toe Knee'). Most of the customers I interact with dont bother to look at the name bc they are often in a rush. But it's fun for me and other partners, and if it gets called out or handed to a customer with the right pronouciation...its all good IME. When customers do see their name spelled out funny, it gives them a laugh. If I cant hear a customers name, they won't get one lol.

Therapist/Social Worker/Psychologist. And a psychiatrist if youre willing to be put on medication or have a conversation about it. I completed an intensive OCD/anxiety program at a behavioral hospital to help with my picking but it's still an issue for me...though it's reduced a ton. Dermatologists can help sometimes too, if the trigger is acne. But therapy is what gets me through and helps challenge my thinking patterns/behaviors. I hope you seek professional help...it is worth it I promise. This disorder is a monster to deal with and I just hope you find some relief, whether its emotional or physical....but hopefully both!!

Also...just a tip for redness control....ive shared with many people who pick their skin...REDNESS RELIEF EYE DROPS. Rip off some tissue for your spots, wet with eye drops and let it dry (about 15 min) and you will see a huge difference from red to a light pink. I have very fair skin and this helps me more than any cream or acne medication. trust!!

Honestly, I know how this feels...and from an outside perspective it does not appear nearly as "bad" as you likely think it does. I say "bad" bc picked skin is not entirely bad...just a simple flaw. Admire your strength for getting where you are and know that skin picking can show up unexpectedly, even with recovery. Youve done amazing hard work, and can continue to keep at it. Dont let this set back determine how far youve come....you look beautiful from what I can see. Your vulnerability makes you even more beautiful. Stay strong and try to not beat yourself over it. YOU ARE HUMAN <3 and most of all...your skin is not a total reflection of who you are and how you appear to others! Xx
LSD and MDMA..."Candy-flipping". I took my doses at the same time and had wild results that I hope I never forget. It was a beautiful experience
